1 Python files do not parse as Python 3, most likely Python 2. A rerun needs a Python 2.7 interpreter (end of life since 2020) or a port, and either is a logged deviation.
Python requirements without an exact version: linearmodels; matplotlib; nlopt; numba; numpy; pandas; scipy; statsmodels. A rerun installs whatever is current and must log the versions it got.
Python code imports srd, which no dependency file names.

The documentation claims a run time of about 160 hours, over this desk's budget of 24 hours (--max-hours). A full rerun needs a compute plan; a partial rerun must say which parts it skipped.
Requires Stata (version 0.12, 0.13, 10.0, 11, 11.0, 13.1, 6.0, 7.0, 8, 8.0, 8.2, 9.2 named in code); the desk says it has it.

Files the code both writes and reads are already in the package: ../C-health dynamics/compas/data/input/key_id_r.dta, ../C-health dynamics/compas/data/input/key_id_sp.dta, ../D-model/inputs/benefits.csv, ../D-model/inputs/hcare_costs.csv, ../D-model/inputs/house_prices_real.csv, ../D-model/inputs/hp.csv, ../D-model/inputs/hp_sp.csv, ../D-model/inputs/know.csv, ../D-model/inputs/ncare_costs.csv, ../D-model/inputs/other_vars.csv. A run may read these instead of recomputing them. A receipt must say whether it replayed them or recomputed them, and a matching output hash alone does not show recomputation.
33 file reads use paths built at run time (macros, globs, variables), so triage could not check that those inputs exist.
The package mentions a cluster or batch scheduler; scripts may assume one.
Non-commercial licence. Rerunning for an editorial check is normally fine; a receipt should not redistribute the package's files.
